s.d: νέκρωσις, -εως, ἡ (νεκρόω), 1. a putting to death. 2. a state of death, death: [[romans 4 19|Rom.4:19]], [[2-corinthians 4 10|2Co.4:10]] (see Deiss., LAE, 94).† (AS)

νέος, -α, -ον [in LXX for נַעַר ([[genesis 37 2|Gen.37:2]], Exo_33:11, al.), חָדָשׁ ([[leviticus 23 16|Lev.23:16]], [[numbers 28 26|Num.28:26]], al.), etc.; compar. -ώτερος for קָטָן, צָעִיר, etc. ;] 1. young, youthful: [[titus 2 4|Tit.2:4.]] 2. new (prop., in respect of time; see: καινός): οἶνος (cf. οἶ. καινός, [[matthew 26 20|Mat.26:20]]), [[matthew 9 17|Mat.9:17]], [[mark 2 22|Mrk.2:22]], [[luke 5 37|Luk.5:37-39]]; φύραμα (figuratively), [[1-corinthians 5 7|1Co.5:7;]] διαθήκη (cf. καινὴ δ., [[hebrews 9 15|Heb.9:15]]), [[hebrews 12 24|Heb.12:24]]; metaphorically, ἄνθρωπος (cf. καινὸς ἀ, [[ephesians 2 15|Eph.2:15]]), [[colossians 3 10|Col.3:10]]. 3. Compar., -ώτερος, -α, -ον, younger: [[luke 15 12|Luk.15:12-13 22:26]], [[john 21 18|Jhn.21:18]]; pl., οἱ ν., [[acts 5 6|Act.5:6]] (Rackham, in l), [[1-timothy 5 11|1Ti.5:11]], [[titus 2 6|Tit.2:6]]; opposite to πρεσβύτεροι, [[1-timothy 5 1|1Ti.5:1]], [[1-peter 5 5|1Pe.5:5]]; αἱ ν., [[1-timothy 5 2|1Ti.5:2 5:14]]. 4. Νέα Πόλις, Neapolis: [[acts 16 11|Act.16:11]] (Rec., Νεάπολις, which see) νεώτερος, see: νέος SYN.: καινός, which see (AS)
νοσσός (νεοσσός, Rec., as in cl. Att.. -ττός; Phryn. rejects the dissyl. form), -οῦ, ὁ (νόος), [in LXX chiefly for בֵּן ;] a young bird: [[luke 2 24|Luk.2:24]] (LXX).† (AS)
νεότης, -ητος, ἡ (νέος), [in LXX chiefly for נָעוּר ;] youth: [[mark 10 20|Mrk.10:20]], [[luke 18 21|Luk.18:21]], [[acts 26 4|Act.26:4]], [[1-timothy 4 12|1Ti.4:12]].† (AS)

νεό-φυτος, -ον (νέος, φύω) [in LXX: [[job 14 9|Job.14:9]], [[psalms 144 12|Psa.144:12]], [[isaiah 5 7|Isa.5:7]] (נֶטַע), [[psalms 128 3|Psa.128:3]] (שְׁתִל)* ;] newly planted (LXX). Metaphorical, as subst., ὁ ν., a new convert, neophyte, novice: [[1-timothy 3 6|1Ti.3:6]]† (AS)
Νέρων, -ωνος, ὁ Nero: 2Ti subscr. (Rec.).† (AS)

νεύω [in LXX: [[proverbs 4 5|Pro.4:5 21:1]] * ;] to nod or beckon, as a sign : with dative of person(s) and inf., [[john 13 24|Jhn.13:24]], [[acts 24 10|Act.24:10]] (cf. δια-, ἐκ-, ἐν-, ἐπι-, κατα-νεύω).† (AS)

νεφέλη, -ης, ἡ (νέφος), [in LXX chiefly for עָנָן, also for עָב, etc. ;] a cloud (single and specific as opposite to νεφος, a great indefinite mass of vapour): [[matthew 17 5|Mat.17:5 24:30 26:64]], [[mark 9 7|Mrk.9:7 13:26 14:62]], [[luke 9 34|Luk.9:34-35 12:54 21:37]], [[acts 1 9|Act.1:9]], [[1-thessalonians 4 17|1Th.4:17]], Ju 12, [[revelation 1 7|Rev.1:7 10:1 11:12 14:14-16]]; of the pillar of cloud in the wilderness ([[exodus 14 19|Exo.14:19-20]], [[psalms 105 39|Psa.105:39]], al.): [[1-corinthians 10 1|1Co.10:1-2]].† (AS)
Νεφθαλείμ (-λίμ, WH in Re, l.with), ὁ indecl. (Heb. נַפְתָּלִי) Naphtali: [[matthew 4 13|Mat.4:13, 15]]" (LXX) [[revelation 7 6|Rev.7:6.]]† (AS)
νέφος, -ους, τό [in LXX for עָב, שַׁחַק, עָנַן ;] a mass of clouds, a cloud (cf. νεφέλη); metaphorically as in Hom., Hdt., al.), of a dense throng: [[hebrews 12 1|Heb.12:1.]]† (AS)

νεφρός, -οῦ, ὁ [in LXX for כִּלְיָה, [[exodus 29 13|Exo.29:13]], al.; metaphorically, [[psalms 7 9|Psa.7:9 16:7 26:2]], Wis.1:6, al. ;] a kidney; pl., the kidneys, reins; metaphorically, of the will and affections: ν. καί καρδίαι (thoughts), [[revelation 2 23|Rev.2:23.]]† (AS)
νεω-κόρος, -ου a temple-keeper; as honorary title given to a city (see DB, i, 722 b) : [[acts 19 35|Act.19:35.]]† (AS)
νεωτερικός, -ή, -όν (νεώτερος), [in LXX: 3Ma.4:8 * ;] = νεανικός, youthful, esp. of qualities: ἐπιθυμίαι, [[2-timothy 2 22|2Ti.2:22]] (Polyb.).† (AS)
νή particle of affirmation employed in oaths, [in LXX: see τ. ὑγίειαν, [[genesis 42 15|Gen.42:15-16]] (חַי) * ;] by: with accusative, [[1-corinthians 15 31|1Co.15:31.]]† (AS)
νήθω [in LXX for טָוָה, שָׁזַר hoph., [[exodus 26 31|Exo.26:31 35:25]], al. ;] to spin: [[matthew 6 28|Mat.6:28]], [[luke 12 27|Luk.12:27]].† (AS)
νηπιάζω (νήπιος), (Hippocr., = νηπιαχεύω, Hom.) to be a babe: [[1-corinthians 14 20|1Co.14:20.]]† (AS)

νήπιος, -α, -ον [in LXX chiefly for עוֹלֵל, also for פְּתִי, etc. ;] infant; of children and minors: [[matthew 21 16|Mat.21:16]] (LXX), [[1-corinthians 13 11|1Co.13:11]], [[galatians 4 1|Gal.4:1]] (see Lft., in l). Metaphorical, childish, unskilled, simple ([[psalms 19 8|Psa.19:8]], [[proverbs 1 32|Pro.1:32]] al.): [[matthew 11 25|Mat.11:25]], [[luke 10 21|Luk.10:21]], [[romans 2 20|Rom.2:20]], [[galatians 4 3|Gal.4:3]], [[ephesians 4 14|Eph.4:14]], [[1-thessalonians 2 7|1Th.2:7]] (WH, fox ἤπιοι); opposite to τέλειος, [[hebrews 5 13|Heb.5:13;]] ν. ἐν Χριστῷ, [[1-corinthians 3 1|1Co.3:1.]]† (AS)
Nereus , a sea-god, son of Πόντος (the sea) , father of the Nereids, (Hesiod) (ML)
Νηρεί (Rec. -ρί), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. נֵרִיָּה), Neri: [[luke 3 27|Luk.3:27.]]† (AS)
νησίον, -ου, τό (dimin. of νῆσος), = νησίς (Hdt., Thuc., al.) a small island: [[acts 27 16|Act.27:16.]]† (AS)
νῆσος, -ου, ὁ [in LXX for אִי ;] an island: [[acts 13 6|Act.13:6 27:26 28:1, 7 28:9, 11]] [[revelation 1 9|Rev.1:9 6:14 16:20]].† (AS)

νηστεία, -ας, ἡ (νηστεύω), [in LXX for צוֹם ;] fasting, a fast; (a) of voluntary abstinence from food: [[matthew 17 21|Mat.17:21]] (WH, R, txt., om.), [[mark 9 29|Mrk.9:29]] (WH, txt., R, txt., om.), [[luke 2 37|Luk.2:37]], [[acts 14 23|Act.14:23]]; of the Day of Atonement, [[acts 27 9|Act.27:9;]] (b) of involuntary abstinence: [[2-corinthians 6 5|2Co.6:5 11:27]].† SYN.: ἀσιτία, q.v (AS)

νηστεύω (νῆστις), [in LXX for צוּם ;] to fast (Arist., Aristoph., al.): [[matthew 4 2|Mat.4:2 6:16-18 9:14-15]] [[mark 2 18|Mrk.2:18-20]], [[luke 5 33|Luk.5:33-35 18:12]], [[acts 13 2|Act.13:2-3]].† (AS)
νῆστις, -ιος, ὁ, ἡ (νη-, neg. prefix, + ἐσθίω), in cl., chiefly poët., [in LXX: Dan LXX 6:18 (19) (טְוָת)* ;] not eating, fasting: [[matthew 15 32|Mat.15:32]], [[mark 8 3|Mrk.8:3]].† (AS)

νηφάλιος (-λεος, Rec., in 1Ti, ll. with), -ον (in cl., -α, -ον), (νήφω), 1. in cl., of drink, not mixed with wine. 2. In later writers (Plut., al.), of persons, sober, temperate: [[1-timothy 3 2|1Ti.3:2 3:11]], [[titus 2 2|Tit.2:2]].† (AS)

νήφω to be sober, abstain from wine; metaphorically, of moral alertness, to be sober, calm, circumspect: [[1-thessalonians 5 6|1Th.5:6 5:8]], [[2-timothy 4 5|2Ti.4:5]] (see Ellic., in l), [[1-peter 1 13|1Pe.1:13 4:7 5:8]] (cf. ἐκ-, ἐκ-νήφω, and see MM, xvii).† SYN.: ἀγρυπνέω, γρηγορέω (AS)
Νίγερ, ὁ (Lat. niger) Niger: [[acts 13 1|Act.13:1.]]† (AS)
Νικάνωρ, -ορος, ὁ Nicanor: [[acts 6 5|Act.6:5.]]† (AS)

νικἀω, -ῶ (νίκη), [in LXX: [[psalms 51 4|Psa.51:4]] (זָכָה), [[proverbs 6 25|Pro.6:25]] frequently (חָמַד); in 4Mac ;] to conquer, prevail: absol., of Christ, [[revelation 3 21|Rev.3:21 6:2]]; C. inf., [[revelation 5 5|Rev.5:5;]] of Christians, [[revelation 2 7|Rev.2:7, 11 2:17, 26 3:5, 12 3:21 21:7]]; before ἐκ (RV, come victorious from), [[revelation 15 2|Rev.15:2;]] as law-term (cl.), [[romans 3 4|Rom.3:4]] (LXX); with accusative of person(s), [[luke 11 22|Luk.11:22]], [[revelation 11 7|Rev.11:7 13:7]] ([WH], R, mg., om.); of Christ, [[john 16 33|Jhn.16:33]] (τ. κόσμον), [[revelation 17 14|Rev.17:14;]] of Christians, [[1-john 4 4|1Jn.4:4;]] τ. πονηρόν, [[1-john 2 13|1Jn.2:13-14;]] αὐτόν (ref. to ὁ κατήγωρ, [[1-john 2 10|1Jn.2:10]]), [[revelation 12 11|Rev.12:11]]; with accusative of thing(s), τὸν κόσμον, [[john 16 33|Jhn.16:33]], [[1-john 5 4|1Jn.5:4-5]]; τὸ κακόν, [[romans 12 21|Rom.12:21;]] pass., μὴ νικῶ ὑπὸ τ. κακοῦ, ib. (cf. ὑπερ-νικάω).† (AS)
νίκη, -ης, ἡ [in LXX: [[1-chronicles 29 11|1Ch.29:11]] (נֶצַח), frequently in 1-4 Mac ;] victory: [[1-john 5 4|1Jn.5:4.]]† (AS)
Νικόδημος, -ου, ὁ Nicodemus: [[john 3 1|Jhn.3:1, 4 3:9 7:50 19:39]].† (AS)
Νικολαΐτης, -αυ, ὁ a Nicolaitan: pl., [[revelation 2 6|Rev.2:6, 15]].† (AS)
Νικόλαος, -αυ, ὁ Nicolaus: [[acts 6 5|Act.6:5.]]† (AS)
Νικόπολις, -εως, ἡ Nicopolis, prob. the city of that name in Epirus (CGT, in l): [[titus 3 12|Tit.3:12]]† (AS)

νῖκος, -ους, τό late form of νίκη, [in LXX: [[lamentations 3 18|La 3:18]] (נֶצַח), I [[esther 3 9|Est.3:9]], 2Ma.10:38, 4Ma.17:12; εἰς ν. (instead of εἰς τέλος, [[job 14 20|Job.14:20]]), [[2-samuel 2 26|2Ki.2:26]], [[job 36 7|Job.36:7]], [[amos 1 11|Amo.1:11 8:7]], [[jeremiah 3 5|Jer.3:5]], [[lamentations 5 20|La 5:20]] (נֶצַח, as נ֝ in Syr., = victory)* ;] victory: [[matthew 12 20|Mat.12:20]] ([[isaiah 42 3|Isa.42:3]], LXX ἀλήθεια), [[1-corinthians 15 54|1Co.15:54]] ([[isaiah 25 8|Isa.25:8]], Aq., Th.), [[1-corinthians 15 55|1Co.15:55]] ([[hosea 13 14|Hos.13:14]], LXX δίκη), [[1-corinthians 15 57|1Co.15:57.]]† (AS)
Νινευΐ, η (Heb. נִינְוֵה), Nineveh: [[luke 11 32|Luk.11:32]], Rec.† (AS)
Νινευείτης (Rec. -ενίτης, L, -ΐτης), -ου, ὁ a Ninevite: [[matthew 12 41|Mat.12:41]], [[luke 11 30|Luk.11:30, 32]].† (AS)
νιπτήρ, -ῆρος, ὁ (νίπτω) a basin: [[john 13 5|Jhn.13:5.]]† (AS)

νίπτω late form of νίζω, [in LXX chiefly for רָחַץ ;] to wash, usually of a part of the body: with accusative of person(s), [[john 13 8|Jhn.13:8;]] τ. πόδας, [[john 13 5|Jhn.13:5-6, 8 13:12, 14]], [[1-timothy 5 10|1Ti.5:10]]; mid., reflexive, to wash oneself: [[john 9 7|Jhn.9:7, 11 9:15]]; τ. χεῖρας, [[matthew 15 2|Mat.15:2]], [[mark 7 3|Mrk.7:3]]; τ. πόδας, [[john 13 10|Jhn.13:10;]] τ. πρόσωπον, [[matthew 6 17|Mat.6:17]] (in cl. Att.. prose, used only in compounds; cf. ἀπο-νίπτω).† νίζω, see: νίπτω SYN.: λούω (which see), πλύνω (AS)

νοιεω νοέω, -ῶ (νοῦς), [in LXX chiefly for בִּין, also for שָׂכַל hi., etc ;] 1. to perceive with the mind, understand (for the phrase νοῶν κ. φρονῶν, in wills, see MM, xvii): absol., [[matthew 16 9|Mat.16:9]], [[mark 8 17|Mrk.8:17]]; with accusative, [[ephesians 3 4|Eph.3:4]], [[1-timothy 1 7|1Ti.1:7]]; with dative instr., τ. καρδίᾳ, [[john 12 40|Jhn.12:40;]] pass., [[romans 1 20|Rom.1:20;]] before ὅτι, [[matthew 15 17|Mat.15:17 16:11]], [[mark 7 18|Mrk.7:18]]; with accusative and inf., [[hebrews 11 8|Heb.11:8.]] 2. to think, consider: absol., [[matthew 24 15|Mat.24:15]], [[mark 13 14|Mrk.13:14]], [[ephesians 3 20|Eph.3:20]]; with accusative of thing(s), [[2-timothy 2 7|2Ti.2:7]] (cf. -εὐ, κατα-, μετα-, προ-, ὑπο-νοέω).† (AS)

νόημα, -τος, τό (νοέω) [in LXX: Sir.21:11, Bar.2:8, 3Ma.5:30 * ;] a thought, purpose, design: [[2-corinthians 2 11|2Co.2:11 10:5 11:3]], [[philippians 4 7|Php.4:7]]. Meton., of the mind, [[2-corinthians 3 14|2Co.3:14 4:4]].† (AS)
νόθος, -η, -ον [in LXX: Wis.4:3 * ;] a bastard, base born, i.e. born of a slave or concubine: [[hebrews 12 8|Heb.12:8.]]† (AS)

νομή, -ῆς, ἡ (νέμω, to pasture), [in LXX chiefly for מִרְעֶה, also for נָוֶה, etc. ;] 1. a pasture, pasturage: figuratively, [[john 10 9|Jhn.10:9]] 2. a grazing, feeding; metaphorically, of a spreading sore, [[2-timothy 2 17|2Ti.2:17]] (Polyb.).† (AS)

νομίζω (νόμος), [in LXX: Wis.13:2 17:3, Sir.29:4, 1-28; 2Ma.4:1-50, 4Ma.8:1-29 * ;] 1. to practise, hold by custom: [[acts 16 13|Act.16:13]] (Rec., but see infr.). 2. to deem, consider, suppose: [[matthew 5 17|Mat.5:17 10:34 20:10]], [[luke 2 44|Luk.2:44 3:23]], [[acts 7 25|Act.7:25 8:20 14:19 16:13, 27 17:29 21:29]], [[1-corinthians 7 26|1Co.7:26 7:36]], [[1-timothy 6 5|1Ti.6:5]].† SYN.: ἡγέομαι, q.v (AS)

νομικός, -ή, -όν (νόμος), [in LXX: 4Ma.5:4 * ;] 1. relating to law: μάχαι, [[titus 3 9|Tit.3:9.]] 2. learned in the law; as subst., ὁ ν. (EV, lawyer): [[matthew 22 35|Mat.22:35]], [[luke 10 25|Luk.10:25]], [[titus 3 13|Tit.3:13]]; pl., [[luke 7 30|Luk.7:30 11:45-46, 52 14:3]] (cf. MM, xvii).† SYN.: γραμματεύς, q.v (AS)
νομίμως adv. (νόμιμος, conformable to law), [in LXX: 4Ma.6:18 * ;] rightly, lawfully: [[1-timothy 1 8|1Ti.1:8]], [[2-timothy 2 5|2Ti.2:5]].† (AS)

νόμισμα, -τος, τό (νομίζω), [in LXX: [[esther 8 36|Est.8:36]] (דָּת), [[nehemiah 7 71|Neh.7:71]] R (דַּרְכְּמוֹן), 1Ma.15:6 * ;] 1. that which is established by usage, a custom. 2. The current coin of a state: [[matthew 22 19|Mat.22:19.]]† (AS)

νομο-διδάσκαλος, -ου, ὁ a teacher of the law: [[luke 5 17|Luk.5:17]], [[acts 5 34|Act.5:34]], [[1-timothy 1 7|1Ti.1:7]] (NT and eccl. only; cf. νομοδείκτης, -διδάκτης, Plut.).† SYN.: γραμματεύς, q.v (AS)
νομοθεσία, -ας, ἡ (νόμος, τίθημι), [in LXX: 2Ma.6:23, 4Ma.5:35 4Mac 17:16 * ;] legislation, lawgiving: [[romans 9 4|Rom.9:4.]]† (AS)

νομοθετέω, -ῶ [in LXX for יָרָה hi. ;] 1. intrans., to make laws; pass., to be furnished with laws: [[hebrews 7 11|Heb.7:11.]] 2. Trans., to ordain by law, enact: pass., [[hebrews 8 6|Heb.8:6.]]† (AS)
νομο-θέτης, -ου, ὁ (νόμος, τίθημι), [in LXX: [[psalms 9 20|Psa.9:20]] * ;] a law­giver: [[james 4 12|Jas.4:12.]]† (AS)

νόμος, -ου, ὁ (νέμω, to deal out, distribute), [in LXX chiefly for תּוֹרָה, also for חֻקָּה, etc. ;] that which is assigned, hence, usage, custom, then law; in NT (only in Mt, Jo, Ja, and the Lucan and Pauline bks.); 1. of law in general: [[romans 3 27|Rom.3:27]] 5:13b; pl., of divine laws, [[hebrews 8 10|Heb.8:10 10:16]]; ὁ ν. τ. Χριστοῦ, [[galatians 6 2|Gal.6:2;]] (τ.) ἐλευθερίας, [[james 1 25|Jas.1:25 2:12]]; βασιλικιός (Hort., in l.; Deiss., LAE, 267:3), [[james 2 8|Jas.2:8.]] 2. Of a force or influence impelling to action: [[romans 7 21|Rom.7:21, 23]]a, 25 8:2. 3. Of the Mosaic law: [[matthew 5 18|Mat.5:18]], [[luke 2 27|Luk.2:27]], [[john 1 17|Jhn.1:17]], [[acts 6 13|Act.6:13]], [[romans 2 15|Rom.2:15]], [[1-corinthians 9 8|1Co.9:8]], [[1-timothy 1 8|1Ti.1:8]], [[hebrews 7 19|Heb.7:19;]] al.; Μωυσέως, [[luke 2 22|Luk.2:22]], [[john 7 23|Jhn.7:23]], [[acts 15 5|Act.15:5]], al.; κυρίου, [[luke 2 39|Luk.2:39;]] κατὰ τὸν ν., [[acts 22 12|Act.22:12]], [[hebrews 7 5|Heb.7:5 9:22]]. 4. As printed, Abbott-Smith mistakenly numbers this as 3.Anarthrous (Bl, §46, 8; ICC on [[romans 2 12|Rom.2:12, 13]]), νόμος, (a) of law in general: [[romans 2 12|Rom.2:12, 14]]b 3:20, 21 4:15, al.; (b) of the Mosaic law in its quality as law: [[romans 2 14|Rom.2:14]]a 5:20 10:4, [[galatians 2 19|Gal.2:19]], al.; οἱ ἐκ ν., [[romans 4 14|Rom.4:14;]] ὑπὸ νόμον, [[1-corinthians 9 20|1Co.9:20]], [[galatians 4 5|Gal.4:5]]; ν. πράσσειν (πληροῦν), [[romans 2 25|Rom.2:25 13:8]]. 5. Of Christian teaching: ν. πίστεως, [[romans 3 27|Rom.3:27;]] τ. Χριστοῦ, [[galatians 6 2|Gal.6:2.]] 6. By meton., of the books which contain the law; (a) of the Pentateuch: [[matthew 12 5|Mat.12:5]], [[john 1 45|Jhn.1:45]], al.; ὁ ν. καὶ οἱ προφῆται, [[matthew 5 17|Mat.5:17]], [[luke 16 16|Luk.16:16]], al.; ὁ ν. καὶ προφῆται κ. ψαλμοί, [[luke 24 44|Luk.24:44.]] (b) of the OT Scriptures in general (as Heb. תּוֹרָה): [[john 10 34|Jhn.10:34 12:34 15:25]], [[1-corinthians 14 21|1Co.14:21]], al. (AS)
νοσέω, -ῶ (νόσος), [in LXX (metaphorically): Wis.17:8 * ;] to be sick: metaphorically, of mental ailment, before περί, [[1-timothy 6 4|1Ti.6:4]] (cf. Plat., Mor., 546 d).† (AS)
νόσημα, -τος, τό (νοσέω), sickness: [[john 5 4|Jhn.5:4.]]† (AS)

νόσος, -ου, ὁ [in LXX for חֲלִי, etc. ;] disease, sickness: [[matthew 4 23|Mat.4:23-24 8:17]] (Aq.) [[matthew 9 35|Mat.9:35 10:1]], [[mark 1 34|Mrk.1:34]], [[luke 4 40|Luk.4:40 6:17 7:21 9:1]], [[acts 19 12|Act.19:12]].† SYN.: see: ἀσθένεια (AS)
νοσσιά, -ᾶς, ἡ (νοσσός), late form of cl., νεοσσιά, [in LXX chiefly for קֵן ;] 1. a nest of birds. 2. a brood of young birds: [[luke 13 34|Luk.13:34.]]† (AS)
νοσσίον, -ου, τό dimin. of νοσσός, which see, [in LXX: [[psalms 84 3|Psa.84:3]] (אֶפְרֹחַ) * ;] a young bird: [[matthew 23 37|Mat.23:37.]]† (AS)

νοσφίζω (νόσφι, apart, aside), [in LXX: [[joshua 7 1|Jos.7:1]] (לָקַח), 2Ma.4:32 * ;] 1. in Hom., as depon., to turn away (from), abandon. 2. After Hom., in act., to set apart, remove. Mid., to set apart for oneself, peculate, purloin: absol., [[titus 2 10|Tit.2:10]] (for ex. in π., see MM, xvii); before ἀπό, [[acts 5 2|Act.5:2-3.]]† (AS)

νότος, -ου, ὁ [in LXX chiefly for נֶגֶב, also for דָּרוֹם, תֵּימָן and קָדִים ;] 1. prop., the south wind: [[luke 12 55|Luk.12:55]], [[acts 27 13|Act.27:13 28:13]] 2. South: [[luke 13 29|Luk.13:29]], [[revelation 21 13|Rev.21:13]] 3. the South, as a region (cf. נֶגֶב): [[matthew 12 42|Mat.12:42]], [[luke 11 31|Luk.11:31]].† (AS)

νότος, -ου, ὁ [in LXX chiefly for נֶגֶב, also for דָּרוֹם, תֵּימָן and קָדִים ;] 1. prop., the south wind: [[luke 12 55|Luk.12:55]], [[acts 27 13|Act.27:13 28:13]] 2. South: [[luke 13 29|Luk.13:29]], [[revelation 21 13|Rev.21:13]] 3. the South, as a region (cf. נֶגֶב): [[matthew 12 42|Mat.12:42]], [[luke 11 31|Luk.11:31]].† (AS)
νουθεσία, -ας ἡ (νουθετέω), = cl. νουθέτησις [in LXX: Wis.6:6 * ;] admonition: [[1-corinthians 10 11|1Co.10:11]], [[ephesians 6 4|Eph.6:4]], [[titus 3 10|Tit.3:10]] (Aristoph., Diod., al.).† (AS)

νουθετέω, -ῶ (νοῦς, τίθημι, hence, put in mind), [in LXX: [[1-samuel 3 13|1Ki.3:13]] (כָּהָה pi.), [[job 8 1|Job.8:1-22]] (יָסַר pi., בִּין), Wis.11:10 12:2, 26 * ;] to admonish, exhort: with accusative of person(s), [[acts 20 31|Act.20:31]], [[romans 15 14|Rom.15:14]], [[1-corinthians 4 14|1Co.4:14]], [[colossians 1 28|Col.1:28 3:16]], [[1-thessalonians 5 12|1Th.5:12 5:14]], [[2-thessalonians 3 15|2Th.3:15]].† (AS)
νεομηνία (Att.. contr., νουμ-, Rec.), -ας, ἡ (νέος, μήν), [in LXX chiefly for חֹדֶשׁ ;] new moon: of the Jewish festival, [[colossians 2 16|Col.2:16.]]† (AS)
νουνεχῶς adv. (νοῦς, ἔχω) sensibly, discreetly: [[mark 12 34|Mrk.12:34.]]† (AS)

νοῦς (contr. from νόος), ὁ, genitive, dative, νοός, νοΐ (late forms, = cl., νοῦ, νῷ; Bl., § 9, 3), accusative, νοῦν, [in LXX chiefly for לֵב, לֵבָב ;] 1. prop., of the ruling faculty, mind, understanding, reason (see Lft., Notes, 88 f.; Vaughan on [[romans 7 23|Rom.7:23]]): [[luke 24 45|Luk.24:45]], [[romans 1 28|Rom.1:28 7:23 12:2 14:5]], [[ephesians 4 17|Eph.4:17, 23]] [[philippians 4 7|Php.4:7]], [[2-thessalonians 2 2|2Th.2:2]], [[1-timothy 6 5|1Ti.6:5]], [[2-timothy 3 8|2Ti.3:8]], [[titus 1 15|Tit.1:15]], [[revelation 13 18|Rev.13:18 17:9]]; ν. τ. σαρκός (ICC, in l), [[colossians 2 18|Col.2:18;]] opposite to σάρξ, [[romans 7 25|Rom.7:25;]] to πνεῦμα, [[1-corinthians 14 14|1Co.14:14-15;]] to γλῶσσα, [[1-corinthians 14 19|1Co.14:19]] 2. By meton., of an act of mind, a mind, thought, purpose: [[romans 11 34|Rom.11:34]] = [[1-corinthians 2 16|1Co.2:16]]" (LXX), [[1-corinthians 1 10|1Co.1:10.]]† νόος, see: νοῦς SYN.: see: πνεῦμα (AS)

Νυμφᾶς, -ᾶ, ὁ (WH, R, mg., Νύμφα, which see), Nymphas: [[colossians 4 15|Col.4:15]], R, txt. (cf. ICC, Lft., in l).† Νύμφα (Rec., R, txt., Νυμφᾶς, which see), -ης, ἡ, Nympha (see M, Pr., 48): [[colossians 4 15|Col.4:15]], WH, R, mg.† (AS)

νύμφη, -ης, ἡ [in LXX chiefly for כַּלָּה ;] 1. cl., a bride, young wife, young woman: [[matthew 25 1|Mat.25:1]], WH, mg., [[john 3 29|Jhn.3:29]], [[revelation 18 23|Rev.18:23 21:2, 9 22:17]]. 2. As frequently in LXX ([[genesis 38 11|Gen.38:11]], al., for כַּלָּה; (a) bride; (b) daughter-in-law) and in MGr. (νύφφη, νύφη), a daughter-in-law: [[matthew 10 35|Mat.10:35]], [[luke 12 53|Luk.12:53]].† (AS)

νυμφίος, -ου, ὁ (νύμφη), [in LXX for חָתָן ;] a bridegroom: [[matthew 9 15|Mat.9:15 25:1, 5-6 25:10]], [[mark 2 19|Mrk.2:19-20]], [[luke 5 34|Luk.5:34-35]], [[john 2 9|Jhn.2:9 3:29]], [[revelation 18 23|Rev.18:23]].† (AS)

νυμφών, -ῶνος, ὁ (νύμφη), [in LXX: Tob.6:13,16* ;] the bride-chamber (Heb. חֻפָּה, LXX, παστός, [[psalms 19 5|Psa.19:5]], [[joel 2 16|Jol.2:16]]): [[matthew 22 10|Mat.22:10]] (WE; γάμος, RV); οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ ν. (cf. cl. νυμφαγωγός, νυμφευτής), the bridegroom's friends who have charge of the nuptial arrangements: [[matthew 9 15|Mat.9:15]], [[mark 2 19|Mrk.2:19]], [[luke 5 34|Luk.5:34]].† (AS)

νῦν, adv., [in LXX chiefly for עַתָּה ;] 1. prop., of time, now, i.e. at the present time: as opposite to past, [[john 4 18|Jhn.4:18]], [[acts 7 52|Act.7:52]], [[romans 13 11|Rom.13:11]], [[2-corinthians 7 9|2Co.7:9]], [[colossians 1 24|Col.1:24]], al.; opposite to fut., [[john 12 27|Jhn.12:27]], [[romans 11 31|Rom.11:31]], al.; with art., ὁ (ἡ, τὸ) and subst., the present: [[romans 3 26|Rom.3:26]], [[galatians 4 25|Gal.4:25]], [[1-timothy 6 17|1Ti.6:17]], [[titus 2 12|Tit.2:12]], al.; απὸ τοῦ ν. (LXX for מֵעַתָּה), [[luke 1 48|Luk.1:48]], [[acts 18 6|Act.18:6]], al.; ἄχρι τοῦ ν., [[romans 8 22|Rom.8:22]], [[philippians 1 5|Php.1:5]]; ἕως τοῦ ν. (LXX for עַד עַתָּה), [[matthew 24 21|Mat.24:21]], [[mark 13 19|Mrk.13:19]]; τὰ ν., as regards the present, [[acts 5 38|Act.5:38;]] with pret., just now, but now, [[matthew 26 65|Mat.26:65]], [[john 11 8|Jhn.11:8 21:10]]; with fut., now, presently, [[john 12 31|Jhn.12:31]], [[acts 20 22|Act.20:22]]; so with praes., presently, forthwith, [[john 12 31|Jhn.12:31 17:13]]; καὶ ν., [[john 11 22|Jhn.11:22 17:5]], al.; ἀλλὰ ν., [[luke 22 36|Luk.22:36;]] ἔτι ν., [[1-corinthians 3 2|1Co.3:2;]] τότε (πότε) . . . ν. (δέ), [[romans 6 21|Rom.6:21 11:30]]; ν. ἤδη, [[1-john 4 3|1Jn.4:3;]] ν. οὖν, [[acts 10 33|Act.10:33]], al. 2. Of logical sequence (often difficult to disting. from the temporal sense; cf. Lft., Notes, 113f.), now, therefore, now, however, as it is: [[luke 11 39|Luk.11:39;]] καὶ ν., [[acts 3 17|Act.3:17]], [[2-thessalonians 2 6|2Th.2:6]], [[1-john 2 28|1Jn.2:28]]; id. before δεῦρο, [[acts 7 34|Act.7:34;]] ν. δέ, [[john 8 40|Jhn.8:40 9:41 15:22, 24, 18:36]], [[1-corinthians 5 11|1Co.5:11 7:14 12:20]], al. (cf. WM, 579.11). (AS)
concerning the present, now

νῦνί an Attic strengthened form of νῦν (in cl. always of time, and most often strictly of the pres.), [in LXX : [[job 5 1|Job.5:1-27]], [[psalms 2 1|Psa.2:1-12, 1-12]], 4Ma.4:1-26, Ep. Je* ;] now; 1. of time: with praes., [[acts 24 13|Act.24:13]], [[romans 15 23|Rom.15:23, 25]], [[1-corinthians 13 13|1Co.13:13]], [[2-corinthians 8 11|2Co.8:11 8:22]], Phm 9 11; with pf., [[romans 3 21|Rom.3:21;]] with pret., [[romans 6 22|Rom.6:22 11:30]] (WH, mg.) [[romans 7 6|Rom.7:6]], [[ephesians 2 13|Eph.2:13]], [[colossians 1 21|Col.1:21 3:8]]; ἡ ν. ἀπολογία, [[acts 22 1|Act.22:1.]] 2. Of logical sequence (not so in cl.): [[romans 7 17|Rom.7:17]], [[1-corinthians 5 11|1Co.5:11]] (νῦν, WH) [[1-corinthians 12 18|1Co.12:18]] (νῦν, WH, txt.) [[1-corinthians 15 20|1Co.15:20]], [[hebrews 8 6|Heb.8:6]] (νῦν, WH, txt.), [[hebrews 9 26|Heb.9:26]] (cf. WM, 24, 579n).† (AS)

νύξ genitive νυκτός, ἡ, [in LXX chiefly for לַיִל ;] night: [[matthew 12 40|Mat.12:40]], [[mark 6 48|Mrk.6:48]], [[john 13 30|Jhn.13:30]], al.; genitive temp. (of the time within which something happens; M, Pr., 73; B1., § 36, 13), νυκτός, by night, [[matthew 2 14|Mat.2:14]], [[john 3 2|Jhn.3:2]], [[1-thessalonians 5 7|1Th.5:7]], al.; ν. κ. ἡμέρας, [[mark 5 5|Mrk.5:5]], [[1-thessalonians 2 9|1Th.2:9]], al.; ἡμέρας κ. ν., [[luke 18 7|Luk.18:7]], [[revelation 4 8|Rev.4:8]], al.; μέσης ν., [[matthew 25 6|Mat.25:6;]] dative, νυκτί, in ans. to the question, "when?" (rare in cl.; Hdt., Soph.), ταύτῃ τ. ν., [[luke 12 20|Luk.12:20]], al.; ἐκείνῃ [[acts 12 6|Act.12:6;]] ἐπιούσῃ, [[acts 23 11|Act.23:11;]] accusative durat. (Bl., § 34, 8; Kühner3, III, 314b), ν. κ. ἠμέραν, [[luke 2 37|Luk.2:37]] [[acts 20 31|Act.20:31]]; τ. νύκτας, [[luke 21 37|Luk.21:37;]] διὰ νυκτός (= cl. νυκτός; Bl., § 42, 1; 46, 7), [[acts 5 19|Act.5:19 16:9 17:10 23:31]]; δι᾽ ὅλης ν., [[luke 5 5|Luk.5:5;]] κατὰ μέσον τῆς ν. (Bl., § 47, 6), [[acts 27 27|Act.27:27.]] Metaphorical: [[john 9 4|Jhn.9:4]], [[romans 13 12|Rom.13:12]], [[1-thessalonians 5 5|1Th.5:5]] (AS)
νύσσω (Att.. -ττω), [in LXX: Sir.22:19, 3Ma.5:14 * ;] to pierce: τ. πλευρὰν λόγχῃ, [[john 19 34|Jhn.19:34]], [[[matthew 27 49|Mat.27:49]]], WH.† (AS)

νυστάζω (cf. νεύω), [in LXX for נוּם, etc ;] to nod in sleep, fall asleep: [[matthew 25 5|Mat.25:5.]] Metaphorical, of negligence or delay, ἡ ἀπώλεια αὐτῶν οὐ νυστάζει (cf. [[psalms 121 4|Psa.121:4]], [[isaiah 5 27|Isa.5:27]]) : [[2-peter 2 3|2Pe.2:3]].† (AS)
νυχθήμερος, -α, -ον (νύξ, ἡμέρα, see B1., § 28, 4), lasting a night and a day; as subst., (τὸ) ν., a night and a day: [[2-corinthians 11 25|2Co.11:25]] (pl., Or. Sib., 8, 203).† (AS)

Νῶε (as LXX, FlJ, who also gives Νώεος, Νῶχος), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. נֹחַ) Noah: [[matthew 24 37|Mat.24:37-38]], [[luke 3 36|Luk.3:36 17:26-27]] [[hebrews 11 7|Heb.11:7]], [[1-peter 3 20|1Pe.3:20]], [[2-peter 2 5|2Pe.2:5]].† (AS)

νωθρός, -ά, -όν [in LXX: [[proverbs 22 29|Pro.22:29]] (חָשֹׁךְ), Sir.4:29 11:12 * ;] sluggish, slothful: [[hebrews 5 11|Heb.5:11 6:12]] (for similar usage in π., see MM, xvii). SYN.: ἀργός (which see), βραδύς (AS)

νῶτος, -ου, ὁ in Att.. most frequently τὸ νῶτον, and in pl. always τὰ νῶτα, [in LXX, ὁ ν., pl., οἱ νῶτοι and τὰ νῶτα, chiefly for כָּתֵף, also for עֹרֶף, מֹתֶן ;] /the back: [[romans 11 10|Rom.11:10]] (LXX).† (AS)

ξενία, -ας, ἡ (ξένος), [in LXX: Sir.29:27 Bl* ;] hospitality, enter­tainment: Phm 22 (cf. ICC, in l, but see infr.). By meton., a place of entertainment, a lodging-place: [[acts 28 23|Act.28:23]], and so perh. Phm 22 (Lft., in l, Phi., p. 9; but see supr., and cf. MM, xvii).† (AS)

ξενίζω (ξένος), [in LXX: [[esther 3 13|Est.3:13]], Sir.29:25, 2Ma.9:6, 3Ma.7:3 * ;] 1. to receive as a guest, entertain: with accusative of person(s), [[acts 10 23|Act.10:23 28:7]], [[hebrews 13 2|Heb.13:2]]; pass., [[acts 10 6|Act.10:6, 18 10:32 21:16]]. 2. In late writers (Polyb., al.; 2Mac, l.with), to surprise, astonish by strangeness: [[acts 17 20|Act.17:20;]] pass., [[1-peter 4 4|1Pe.4:4 4:12]].† (AS)
ξενοδοχέω late Gk. for -κέω (ξένος, δέχομαι), to entertain strangers: [[1-timothy 5 10|1Ti.5:10.]]† (AS)

ξένος, -η, -ον [in LXX chiefly for נׇכְרִי ;] (a) foreign, alien: δαιμόνια, [[acts 17 18|Act.17:18;]] διδαχαί [[hebrews 13 9|Heb.13:9;]] (b) with genitive of thing(s), strange to, estranged from, ignorant of: [[ephesians 2 12|Eph.2:12;]] (with) strange, unusual: [[1-peter 4 12|1Pe.4:12.]] As subst., ὁ ξ., (a) a foreigner, stranger: [[matthew 25 35|Mat.25:35, 38 25:43-44 27:7]], [[acts 17 21|Act.17:21]], 3Jn.5; ξέίνοι κ. τάροικοι (opposite to συμπολῖται, οίκεῖοι), [[ephesians 2 19|Eph.2:19;]] ξ. καὶ παρεπίδημοι, [[hebrews 11 13|Heb.11:13;]] (b) one of the parties bound by ties of hospitality; α the guest; β the host (= ξενοδόκος, Hom., Ii, xv, 532) : [[romans 16 23|Rom.16:23.]]† (AS)

ξέστης, -ου, ὁ (a Sicilian corruption of Lat. sextarius), [in Al. : [[leviticus 14 10|Lev.14:10]] (לֹג, LXX κοτύλη)* ;] 1. a sextarius (about a pint). 2. In NT, a pitcher of wood or stone : [[mark 7 4|Mrk.7:4.]]† (AS)

ξηραίνω (ξηρός), [in LXX chiefly for יָבֵשׁ ;] to dry up, parch, wither. with accusative, τ. χόρτον, [[james 1 11|Jas.1:11;]] pass., to become or be dry or withered. of plants, [[matthew 13 6|Mat.13:6 21:19-20]], [[mark 4 6|Mrk.4:6 11:20-21]], [[luke 8 6|Luk.8:6]], [[john 15 6|Jhn.15:6]], [[1-peter 1 24|1Pe.1:24]]; of ripened crops, [[revelation 14 15|Rev.14:15;]] of liquids, [[mark 5 20|Mrk.5:20]], [[revelation 16 12|Rev.16:12]]; of members of the body, to waste away, [[mark 3 1|Mrk.3:1]] (cf. 3Ki.13:4) [[mark 9 18|Mrk.9:18]].† (AS)

ξηρός, -ά, -όν [in LXX chiefly for יָבֵשׁ, its parts and deriva­tives, also for חָרָבָה, etc. ;] dry: metaphorically (of a sinner), ξύλον ξ., [[luke 23 31|Luk.23:31;]] of members of the body shrunken by disease, withered: [[john 5 3|Jhn.5:3;]] of the hand, [[matthew 12 10|Mat.12:10]] [[mark 3 3|Mrk.3:3]], [[luke 6 6|Luk.6:6]], 8; of the dry land, ἡ ξηρά (sc. γῆ, cf. [[genesis 1 9|Gen.1:9-10;]] [[jonah 1 19|Jon.1:19]], al.): [[matthew 23 15|Mat.23:15]]; γῆ, [[hebrews 11 29|Heb.11:29.]]† (AS)
ξύλινος, -η, -ον (ξύλον) [in LXX chiefly for עֵץ ;] wooden: [[2-timothy 2 20|2Ti.2:20]], [[hebrews 9 20|Heb.9:20]] (cf. Ep. [[jeremiah 4 1|Jer.4:1-31]] ff).† (AS)

ξύλον, -ου, τό [in LXX chiefly for עֵץ ;] 1. wood: [[1-corinthians 3 12|1Co.3:12]], [[revelation 18 12|Rev.18:12]]. 2. a piece of wood, hence, anything made of wood, as, (a) a cudgel, staff: pl., [[matthew 26 47|Mat.26:47, 55]], [[mark 14 43|Mrk.14:43, 48]], [[luke 22 52|Luk.22:52]]; (b) stocks, for confining the feet ([[job 33 11|Job.33:11]], סַד) : [[acts 16 24|Act.16:24;]] (with) a beam to which malefactors were bound (late Gk.), in LXX, of a gibbet ([[deuteronomy 21 22|Deu.21:22-23]]), in NT, of the Cross: [[acts 5 30|Act.5:30 10:39 13:29]], [[galatians 3 13|Gal.3:13]], [[1-peter 2 24|1Pe.2:24]]. 3. In late writers (see MM, xvii), a tree ([[genesis 1 29|Gen.1:29]], [[isaiah 14 8|Isa.14:8]], al.) : [[luke 23 31|Luk.23:31]]; ξ. τῆς ζωῆς, [[revelation 2 7|Rev.2:7 22:2, 14 22:19]].† (AS)

ξυράω, -ῶ late form of ξυρέω (which see) : [[1-corinthians 11 6|1Co.11:6]] (ξυρᾶσθαι, Rec. and Edd., but see: ξύρω).† ξύρω, rare form of ξυρέω (Veitch, see word), aor. mid., ξύρασθαιι (Bl., § 24, see word; Zorell, see word, etc.) for -ᾶσθαι (Rec., Edd.) : [[1-corinthians 11 6|1Co.11:6.]]† (AS)

ὁ, ἡ, τό, the prepositive article (ἄρθρον προτακτικόν), originally a demonstr. pron. (so usually in Hom.), in general corresponding to the Eng. definite article. I. As demonstr. pron. 1. As frequently in Hom., absol., he (she, it), his (etc.): [[acts 17 28|Act.17:28]] (quoted from the poet Aratus). 2. Distributive, ὁ μὲν . . . ὁ δέ, the one . . . the other: [[1-corinthians 7 7|1Co.7:7]], [[galatians 4 22|Gal.4:22]]; pl., [[acts 14 4|Act.14:4, 17:32]], [[philippians 1 16|Php.1:16]], al.; οἱ μὲν . . . ἄλλοι δέ, [[matthew 16 14|Mat.16:14]], [[john 7 12|Jhn.7:12]]; οἱ μεν̀ . . . ὁδέ, [[hebrews 7 21|Heb.7:21, 23]]. 3. In narration (without ὁ μὲν preceding), ὁ δέ, but he: [[matthew 2 14|Mat.2:14]], [[mark 1 45|Mrk.1:45]], [[luke 8 21|Luk.8:21]], [[john 9 38|Jhn.9:38]], al. mult. II. As prepositive article, the, prefixed, 1. to nouns unmodified: ὁ θεός, τὸ φῶς, etc.; to abstract nouns, ἡ σοφία, etc., to pl. nouns which indicate a class, οἱ ἀλώπεκες, foxes, [[matthew 8 20|Mat.8:20]], al.; to an individual as representing a class, ὁ ἐργάτης, [[luke 10 7|Luk.10:7;]] with nom. = voc. in addresses, [[matthew 11 26|Mat.11:26]], [[john 19 3|Jhn.19:3]], [[james 5 1|Jas.5:1]], al.; to things which pertain to one, ἡ χεῖρ, his hand, [[mark 3 1|Mrk.3:1;]] to names of persons well known or already mentioned; usually to names of countries (originally adjectives), ἡ Ἰουδαία, etc. 2. To modified nouns: with of person(s) pron. genitive, μοῦ, σοῦ, etc.; with poss. pron., ἐμός, σός, etc.; with adj. between the art. and the noun, ὁ ἀγαθὸς ἄνθρωπος, [[matthew 12 35|Mat.12:35;]] the noun foll, by adj., both with art., ὁ ποιμὴν ὁ καλός, [[john 10 11|Jhn.10:11]] (on ὁ ὄχλος πολύς, [[john 12 9|Jhn.12:9]], see M, Pr., 84); before adjectival phrases, ἡ κατ᾽ ἐκλογὴν πρόθεσις, [[romans 9 11|Rom.9:11.]] 3. To Other parts of speech used as substantives; (a) neuter adjectives: τ. ἀγαθόν, etc.; (b) cardinal numerals: ὁ εἶς, οἷ δύο, etc.; (with) participles: ὁ βαπτίζων (= ὁ Βαπτιστής, [[matthew 14 2|Mat.14:2]]), [[mark 6 14|Mrk.6:14]]; πᾶς ὁ, with ptcp., every one who, etc.; (d) adverbs: τὸ πέραν, τὰ νῦν, ὁ ἔσω ἄνθρωπος; (e) infinitives: nom., τὸ θέλειν, [[romans 7 18|Rom.7:18]], al.; genitive, τοῦ, after adjectives, ἄξιον τοῦ πορεύεσθαι, [[1-corinthians 16 4|1Co.16:4;]] verbs, ἐλαχεν τοῦ θυμιᾶσαι, [[luke 1 9|Luk.1:9;]] and frequently in a final sense, ἐξῆλθεν ὁ σπείρειν, [[matthew 13 3|Mat.13:3]] (on the artic. inf., see Bl., §71). 4. In the neut. to sentences, phrases or single words treated as a quotation: τὸ Ἐι δύνῃ, [[mark 9 23|Mrk.9:23;]] τὸ ἔτι ἅπαξ, [[hebrews 12 27|Heb.12:27;]] τὸ ἀνέβη, [[ephesians 4 9|Eph.4:9]], al. 5. To prepositional phrases: οἱ ἀπὸ Ἰταλίας, [[hebrews 13 24|Heb.13:24;]] οἱ ἐκ νόμου, [[romans 4 14|Rom.4:14;]] neut. accusative absol., in adverbial phrases, τὸ καθ᾽ ἡμέραν, daily, [[luke 11 3|Luk.11:3;]] τὸ κατὰ σάρκα, as regards the flesh, [[romans 9 5|Rom.9:5.]] 6. To nouns in the genitive, denoting kinship, association, etc.: ὁ τοῦ, the son of (unless context indicates a different relationship), [[matthew 10 2|Mat.10:2]], al.; τὰ τοῦ θεοῦ, the things that pertain to God, [[matthew 16 23|Mat.16:23;]] τὰ τῆς εἰρήνης, [[romans 14 19|Rom.14:19]] (cf. M, Pr., 81ff.; Bl, §§46, 47). (AS)
eighty , Lat. octoginta, (Thucydides), etc.:—;ionic and doric ὀγδώκοντα, (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

ὄγδοος, -η, -ον the eighth. [[luke 1 59|Luk.1:59]], [[acts 7 3|Act.7:3]]" (LXX), [[revelation 17 11|Rev.17:11 21:20]]; one of eight, with seven others (usually, in this sense, with αὐτός added, but cf. Plat., Legg., iii, 695 with; Plut., Pelop., 13; 2Ma.5:27): [[2-peter 2 5|2Pe.2:5]].† (AS)
ὄγκος, -ου, ὁ bulk, mass; metaphorically, an encumbrance: [[hebrews 12 1|Heb.12:1.]]† SYN.: βάρος, a weight; φορτίον, a burden, that which is borne (AS)

ὅδε, ἥδε, τόδε (the old demonstr. pron., ὁ + the enclitic δε), = Lat. hicce, this (here), referring prop, to what is present, can be seen or pointed out: of a person just named, τῇδε (= ταύτῃ), [[luke 10 39|Luk.10:39;]] neut. pl., τάδε (λέγει), referring to words which follow (so in Att.., and see MM, xvii) : [[acts 21 11|Act.21:11]], [[revelation 2 1|Rev.2:1, 8 2:12, 18 3:1, 7 3:14]]; εἰς τήνδε τ. πόλιν (= Att.. τῇ καὶ τῇ, Plat., Legg., iv, 721 B), such and such a city, [[james 4 13|Jas.4:13.]]† (AS)
ὁδεύω (ὁδός), [in LXX : [[1-kings 6 12|3Ki.6:12]] A (metaphorically, הָלַךְ), Tob.6:5, Wis.5:7 (figuratively)* ;] to travel, journey: [[luke 10 33|Luk.10:33]] (cf.δι-, συν-οδεύω).† (AS)

ὁδηγέω, -ῶ, (ὁδηγός) [in LXX chiefly for נוּחַ, also for דֶּרֶךְ hi., הָלַךְ hi., etc. ;] to lead on one's way, to guide: with accusative of person(s), [[matthew 15 14|Mat.15:14]], [[luke 6 39|Luk.6:39;]] id. before ἐπί, [[revelation 7 17|Rev.7:17.]] Metaphorical, to guide, instruct, teach: [[acts 8 31|Act.8:31;]] before εἰς τ. ἀλήθειαν (ἐν τ. ἀ., WH, mg.), [[john 16 13|Jhn.16:13]] (cf. [[psalms 25 5|Psa.25:5]]).† (AS)

ὁδηγός, -οῦ, ὁ (ὁδός, ἡγέομαι) [in LXX : [[esther 8 1|Est.8:1]], Wis.7:15 18:3, 1Ma.4:2, 2Ma.5:15 * ;] a leader on the way, a guide: [[acts 1 16|Act.1:16.]] Fig., ὁ. τυφλῶν, [[romans 2 19|Rom.2:19;]] pl., [[matthew 15 14|Mat.15:14 23:16, 24]].† (AS)
ὁδοιπορέω, -ῶ (ὁδοιπόρος, a traveller, [[genesis 37 25|Gen.37:25]], al.), to travel, journey: [[acts 10 9|Act.10:9.]]† (AS)
ὁδοιπορία, -ας, ἡ (see supr.), [in LXX : Wis.13:18 18:3 19:5, 1Ma.6:41 * ;] a journey. [[john 4 6|Jhn.4:6]], [[2-corinthians 11 26|2Co.11:26]].† (AS)

ὁδός, -οῦ, ἡ, [in LXX chiefly (very freq.) for דֶּרֶךְ ;] 1. a way, path, road: [[matthew 2 12|Mat.2:12]], [[mark 10 46|Mrk.10:46]], [[luke 3 5|Luk.3:5]] al.; κατὰ τὴν ὁ., [[luke 10 4|Luk.10:4]], al.; παρὰ τὴν ὁ., [[matthew 13 4|Mat.13:4]], al.; with genitive of person(s), (subj.), τὴν ὁ. ἑτοιμάζειν (fig.), [[matthew 3 3|Mat.3:3]], [[mark 1 3|Mrk.1:3]], al.; with genitive term. (obj.), ἐθνῶν, [[matthew 10 5|Mat.10:5;]] τ. ἁγίων (figuratively), [[hebrews 9 8|Heb.9:8;]] accusative, ὁδόν, with force of prep. (like Heb. דֶּרֶךְ; Bl., §34, 8; 35, 5), ὁ. θαλάσσης, [[matthew 4 15|Mat.4:15]] (LXX). 2. A traveller's way, journey: ἐν τ. ὁ., [[matthew 5 25|Mat.5:25]], [[mark 8 27|Mrk.8:27]], al.; ἐξ ὁ., [[luke 11 6|Luk.11:6;]] εἰς ὁ., [[matthew 10 10|Mat.10:10;]] τ. ὁδὸν πορεύεσθαι, [[acts 8 39|Act.8:39;]] ὁ. ἡμέρας, [[luke 2 44|Luk.2:44;]] ὁδὸν ποιεῖν (= cl., ὁ. ποιεῖσθαι; V. Field, Notes, 25), to make one's way, i.e. proceed on one's journey, [[mark 2 23|Mrk.2:23.]] 3. Metaphorical (cl.; but esp. frequently in Heb.; see Cremer, 442ff.), of a course of conduct, a way of thinking or acting: [[acts 14 16|Act.14:16]], [[1-corinthians 4 17|1Co.4:17 12:31]], [[james 1 8|Jas.1:8 5:20]]; τοῦ Κάϊν, Ju 11; τ. Βαλαάμ, [[2-peter 2 15|2Pe.2:15;]] εἰρήνης, [[romans 3 17|Rom.3:17;]] ζωῆς, [[acts 2 28|Act.2:28;]] ἡ ὁ. ἡ ἀπάγουσα εἰς τ. ζωήν (Dalman, Words, 160), [[matthew 7 14|Mat.7:14;]] τ. δικαιοσύνης, [[matthew 21 32|Mat.21:32;]] σωτηρίας, [[acts 16 17|Act.16:17;]] αἱ ὁ. τ. θεοῦ (κυρίου), [[acts 13 10|Act.13:10]], [[romans 11 33|Rom.11:33]], [[revelation 15 3|Rev.15:3]] (cf. [[hosea 14 9|Hos.14:9]] Psa.94 (95):10, Sir.39:24, al.); ἡ ὁ. τ. θεοῦ (the way approved by God), [[matthew 22 16|Mat.22:16]], [[mark 12 14|Mrk.12:14]], [[luke 20 21|Luk.20:21]]; id., of the Christian religion, [[acts 18 26|Act.18:26;]] so, absol., ἡ ὁ., [[acts 9 2|Act.9:2 19:9, 23 24:22]]; of Christ as the means of approach to God, [[john 14 6|Jhn.14:6.]] 4. Ellipsis of ὁ.: ποίας (sc. ὁδοῦ), [[luke 5 19|Luk.5:19;]] ἐκείνης, [[luke 19 4|ib. 19:4]] (see Bl., §36, 13; 44, 1). (AS)

ὀδούς, -όντος, ὁ [in LXX for שֵׁן ;] a tooth: [[matthew 5 38|Mat.5:38]], [[mark 9 18|Mrk.9:18]], [[acts 7 54|Act.7:54]]; pl., [[revelation 9 8|Rev.9:8]], ὁ βρυγμὸς (which see) τ. ὀδόντων, [[matthew 8 12|Mat.8:12 13:42, 50 22:13 24:51 25:30]], [[luke 13 28|Luk.13:28]].† (AS)
